title: Change-in-Law Pass-Through Rights by C&I Structure
content:
Under Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts, whether a fixed price may be adjusted during the term for a change in law or regulation depends on the structure, and every structure sets the same minimum notice between a pass-through notice and its effective date.

| Structure | Fixed price may be adjusted for a change in law or regulation | Minimum calendar days between the pass-through notice and its effective date |
|---|---|---|
| Beacon Ridge C&I Real-Time Index | no | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge C&I Block and Index | yes | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge C&I Fixed Energy with Capacity and Transmission Pass-Through | yes | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge C&I Fixed Energy with Capacity Pass-Through | yes | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge C&I Fixed All-In | yes | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge C&I Fixed All-In Renewable | no | 30 |

## Points of reading

- Four structures carry the change-in-law right: Block and Index, the two Fixed Energy structures and Fixed All-In.
- Real-Time Index and Fixed All-In Renewable do not; on those two structures the price may not be adjusted for a change in law or regulation.
- The notice minimum is counted in calendar days: a notice dated 1 May is 30 calendar days ahead of an effective date of 31 May, and 29 days ahead of an effective date of 30 May (dates hypothetical).
